\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Photovoltaic electroluminescence inspection requires image review and crack localization under limited annotation and acquisition shift. We compare frozen DINOv3 representations, low-rank adaptation (LoRA), full fine-tuning, CNNs, normal references and local published-architecture ports with explicit label and optimization budgets. One frozen registry retains 1,061 model/inference views in 427 recipe families, yielding 1,683 prediction jobs and 6,212 declared endpoint contrasts. On matching SCDD acquisition-held-source confirmation strata, LoRA has higher image AUROC than the adapted CNN in all six source/budget conditions and all eighteen fitted pairs; positive-image Dice is lower in four of six conditions. Under matched UCF supervision of 86 training and 144 validation masks, LoRA obtains mean confirmation Dice 0.485 versus 0.369 for the full supervised local port, with conditional unadjusted difference interval [0.088, 0.148]. The same comparison transfers to SCDD with lower mean Dice despite higher AUROC. On restricted PVEL, full-budget SCDD LoRA reaches known-crack recall 0.952 while misclassifying an author-normal fraction 0.854 at its source threshold. Reference, ensemble and optimization effects vary by endpoint and cohort; fewer trainable parameters do not guarantee faster inference. All registered contrasts, seeds, native-failure strata and fixed population sensitivities are retained. The results support evaluating recognition, native overlap and operating-point transfer jointly. Intervals condition on fitted systems and are unadjusted; reused development exposure, unequal pretraining/optimization and unverified physical grouping preclude universal architecture superiority or operational reliability claims.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Electroluminescence (EL) images support photovoltaic inspection by exposing spatial patterns associated with cracks and other defects. A useful inspection system must help decide which images require review and where crack evidence occurs. These objectives require different annotations and can disagree: an image can receive a high crack score while its predicted mask misses a thin crack, and a system can localize part of a crack while flagging many crack-negative images. An evaluation based only on image AUROC leaves these distinctions unresolved.

Large pretrained visual encoders offer a practical way to fit small EL datasets. DINOv3 supplies frozen global and patch representations~\cite{dinov3}; low-rank adaptation (LoRA) updates a restricted set of encoder weights~\cite{lora}. Their usefulness depends on annotation requirements, optimization, acquisition conditions and the downstream task. Different pretraining corpora and different training objectives prevent a causal interpretation of an observed DINOv3--CNN difference as an architecture effect.

Our study asks three questions. First, how do frozen features, LoRA and full fine-tuning behave as training-label availability changes? Second, do image-level gains accompany native-resolution crack recovery and acceptable source-frozen review decisions? Third, does local normal-reference information improve a matched dense predictor across acquisition sources? We retain full supervised and semi-supervised local published-architecture ports, classical feature controls, stronger CNN optimization sensitivities and adverse fitted seeds to test these questions.

Nominal-feature matching is established prior work. PatchCore uses pretrained local features and representative memory~\cite{patchcore}; AnomalyDINO develops frozen DINOv2 patch-based anomaly detection~\cite{anomalydino}; and SuperADD already combines DINOv3 and nominal-feature memory in an industrial workshop-challenge report~\cite{superadd}. We do not claim the first use of DINOv3, EL transfer or local normal memory. DINOv2 is reviewed as prior art and is not executed. Our contribution is the controlled, crack-specific assessment of supervision, native localization, operating decisions and acquisition transfer, including failures. Published scores on different datasets and ontologies are not used as a performance ranking.

\section{Data and evaluation design}
\subsection{Cohorts, annotations and exposure}
Table~\ref{tab:main_cohorts} separates development from the fixed confirmation populations. SCDD contributes 588 audited real images from ARTS, CFVS and CSIR~\cite{pratt}. Its internal split contains 351 training, 120 validation and 117 confirmation images, with 156, 54 and 53 annotated crack positives, respectively. Provided capture-family prefixes define grouping units; physical module identity has not been verified. Whole fields of view are retained. A crack-positive label means an explicit crack annotation in the field, not measured electrical failure or central-cell power loss. Crack-negative images may contain other defects.

SCDD & 351 train + 120 validation; 117 confirmation & Three acquisition channels. Matching held-source primary strata contain ARTS 43, CFVS 27 and CSIR 47 images. Provided families are not verified modules.\\

\end{table}

UCF training and validation labels support source hyperparameter selection~\cite{fioresi}. Their reuse by later SCDD-fitted systems means SCDD-to-UCF 507 is sample-disjoint prediction in a development-exposed dataset, rather than selection on a never-observed dataset. SCDD development also informs study-wide methodological choices. A UCF-only gradient-fit history therefore does not make SCDD unseen to the research process. We retain gradient-fit, validation, upstream hyperparameter and unlabelled-image exposure separately.

The PVEL task restricts positives to explicitly annotated crack/star-crack images and negatives to author-normal images~\cite{pvelad}. Unlabelled official-test images and uncertain crack-negative other-defect images do not enter specificity claims. A prospective whole-frame integrity audit reviewed 15,963 images and retained 17 strong within-PVEL near-copy pairs. Their 34 members are excluded from the primary view. The full 12,326-image pool and a broader 11,927-image exclusion view remain sensitivities derived from the same saved predictions. Physical recapture history, all cropped overlaps and pretraining membership remain unknown. These constructed populations do not estimate operational prevalence.

\subsection{Annotation budgets and native task definitions}
Internal SCDD training budgets use 18, 36, 70 or 351 images, corresponding to approximately 5\%, 10\%, 20\% and 100\% of the training pool. The same 120 validation labels are additional supervision. Subsets are nested within seed and use the audited labels for class stratification; they do not measure prospective annotation time. The matched UCF 20\% comparison uses 86 training masks and 144 validation masks per fit, all contained within the 574-image development/HPO pool. They are not 230 plus 574 distinct labelled images.

Canonical pixel labels distinguish crack, normal and other intrinsic defects while excluding the specified border, text, padding and measurement-artifact categories. UCF unknown index 128 remains ignored. Pixel-loss eligibility differs from image validity: ignored regions remain visible in the input. Narrow SCDD crack masks and broader UCF annotation regions can produce different native pixel scores. Acquisition, content, annotation extent and class composition are not separately identified causes in this study.

\subsection{Frozen confirmation and uncertainty}
After all original fitting, full-method, efficiency and supplementary ELPV schedules completed, a complete source review fixed one registry. It retains 1,061 model/inference-view records in 427 recipe families: 317 three-seed families and 110 deterministic full-budget singletons. These are not 1,061 newly trained models or 427 architectures. Teacher 1 and ensemble inference share training; deterministic reuse and overlapping source cohorts do not create independent replications.

The registry declares 1,683 model/cohort jobs and 6,212 endpoint contrasts. All models, thresholds, source temperatures, preprocessing, memories, score directions, populations, examples and scientific evaluator bytes were fixed before predictive access on 27 October 2026. Predictions and the complete saved-output audit finished on 28 October. No target outcome may select a replacement model, endpoint or example. The complete statistical output and ordered reporting review are now available; no scientific choices were altered using these outcomes.

Image discrimination uses AUROC and average precision (AP), with recall, false-positive rate (FPR) and flagged review fraction at the source-selected threshold. AP follows the average-precision definition. Localization uses whole-cohort pooled native pixel AP, positive-image Dice/IoU and eligible normal-structure FPR. PVEL known-crack recall, author-normal FPR and box-point hit rate retain their narrower meanings. Unsupported endpoints remain not estimable; UCF normal-structure FPR is not replaced with a different negative-field endpoint.

Each declared difference is SECOND family minus FIRST family. Where supported, 1,000 paired resamples of provided acquisition families yield conditional percentile intervals for the mean fitted-pair difference. Seeds 11, 22 and 33 remain individually reported. Intervals are unadjusted across the large comparison family, conditional on these fitted systems, and do not represent training-population or independent-domain uncertainty. Native pooled pixel AP is a whole-cohort point estimate, without pixel pseudoreplication. PVEL receives no invented capture-family interval. The fixed native-failure policy retains crack-area bins at 0.5\% and 2\%, all positives and all negatives, including empty-denominator nulls.

Figure~\ref{fig:main_design} connects the source-label and selection exposures to the single frozen prediction workflow. Complete aggregate source and cost figures are retained in the separate fourteen-page numerical source companion.

\section{Models and controls}
Whole grayscale images are replicated to three channels, bicubically letterboxed to 336 pixels and normalized using the corresponding pretrained-model convention. DINOv3-S/16 supplies 384-dimensional global and patch vectors; register tokens are excluded from patch pooling. Image-only systems use frozen DINOv3, LoRA or full fine-tuning, with fully adapted ResNet-18, ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-B0 controls~\cite{resnet,efficientnet}. LoRA uses rank 8 and scaling 8 on query/value projections in the last four transformer blocks. Image heads are linear; pretrained CNN batch-normalization statistics stay fixed while affine parameters remain trainable.

Source-only hyperparameter selection and checkpoint rules precede confirmation. Image systems use AdamW~\cite{adamw}, synchronized whole-field D4 views and source-validation AUROC stopping. Source validation also fits temperature scaling~\cite{calibration} and the high-recall image operating point. Stronger image-CNN learning-rate controls remain source optimization sensitivities. Frozen CLS, patch-mean, concatenated, scale and larger-encoder probes, plus HOG/statistics logistic and SVM controls~\cite{hog,svm}, remain separate complete systems with unequal search budgets.

Dense DINOv3 reads depths 3, 6, 9 and 12 with a multiscale decoder and detail skips. The adapted DeepLabv3+/ResNet-50 comparator~\cite{deeplab} and DINO systems use image BCE, weighted three-class pixel CE and 0.5 times crack soft-Dice loss. Class weights use inverse-square-root source frequencies. The source checkpoint statistic samples at most 8,192 fixed known transformed pixels per validation image; selected checkpoints are evaluated at native resolution. Matching original mask identities does not match pretraining or optimizer work.

The normal-reference arm uses only selected training masks. A frozen-CLS coverage rule selects at most 256 reference images; each query retrieves five and excludes its entire provided capture family. Normalized patch matching minimizes
\begin{equation}
1-q^{\mathsf T}r+0.1\lVert p_q-p_r\rVert_2^2.
\end{equation}
The local input contains query features, query-minus-reference residuals, coordinates and cosine distance. The image head fuses global vectors with top 5\% local crack evidence. Reference-free, no-position and mean-evidence controls retain the relevant architectural constraints. Both frozen reference conditions contain 1,387,269 trainable parameters; the LoRA encoder adds 49,152 parameters. A separate capped normal-distance control uses its frozen source noncrack cutoff and is not a calibrated crack posterior. Its cutoff differs from learned softmax threshold 0.5.

Additional controls use a last-layer patch MLP and a frozen post-LoRA encoder with newly trained reference/no-reference decoder heads. Extra adaptation and fresh-head stages are charged as computation; matching masks does not isolate a matching-specific cause. The full supervised and semi-supervised ports retain the released PS-MT/PV-S3 architecture~\cite{psmt,pvs3}, with separately documented three-class whole-field adaptation, teacher-decoder VAT, weak/strong views, CutMix and EMA consistency~\cite{vat,cutmix,meanteacher}. Teacher 1 is primary; the fixed teacher-ensemble view is correlated. A literal numerical VAT sensitivity is retained. These are local ports under our protocol, not reproductions of the published headline score. Complete recipes, source-fit counts, source failures and attribution appear in the supplementary record.

\subsection{Optimization work and source exposure}
Image-only neural fits use batches of eight; joint dense, patch, fresh-head and full-port fits use batches of two. The image and joint dense pipelines use AdamW with weight decay $10^{-4}$, 50 updates per round, at most 40 rounds and patience six. The full architecture ports use SGD with momentum 0.9, weight decay $10^{-4}$ and polynomial learning-rate decay. Their round length is $\max(50,\lceil N_{\mathrm{source}}/2\rceil)$ updates, using the entire source-training pool size even for a partially labelled supervised subset. Table~\ref{tab:main_optimization} reports actual saved update counts. These are unequal optimization budgets, rather than matched-compute tests of backbones.

\section{Source development and computational context}
All original source schedules finished before confirmation. The complete source record retains every selected and adverse fitted seed, all ten SCDD dense development conditions, matched UCF controls, full architecture ports, representation/optimization sensitivities and reference mechanisms. Source image AUROC and native crack overlap already disagreed: full-budget internal LoRA had Dice 0.149 versus 0.198 for the adapted CNN despite higher image AUROC. The stronger image-only ResNet-50 optimization sensitivity reached source AUROC 0.969 versus 0.956 for image-only LoRA. Neither source comparison was used to replace a model after confirmation access.

The 97-case formal benchmark contains 388 cohort/batch conditions and 1,164 uninstrumented cohort passes on the 32 GiB M2 Max. Full-budget dense LoRA averages 31.73 ms/image on SCDD at batch one versus 27.08 for the adapted CNN, with mixed fitted-pair timing directions. These cases do not independently benchmark every later confirmation checkpoint. RSS lifetime highwater and sampled MPS tensor/driver allocations remain separate overlapping observations. The separate ELPV development supplement has 24 outer fits and 480 inner-grid fits: DINOv3 CLS plus RBF SVM has mean outer AUROC 0.904918 versus 0.838261 for HOG/statistics plus RBF SVM. Overlapping grouped folds and expert-review labels do not provide crack-localization or independent CNN confirmation. The 656 course-test images remain unscored. Complete source values and figures are preserved in the supplementary record.

\section{Confirmation results}\label{sec:main_confirmation_complete}
All 1,683 frozen prediction jobs, their saved-output audits and all 6,212 declared endpoint contrasts are complete. Every declared contrast is estimable in its registered scope; this does not make every per-job endpoint available. UCF normal-structure FPR remains null, and 116 of the 2,480 native-failure subgroups have empty denominators and null rates. The complete reporting record contains all 16,140 original fitted-pair records, 3,686 absolute family/endpoint cells and all 29 overlapping control-question themes. Tables below summarize original central controls; the exhaustive atlas and numeric companions retain every other contrast, interval, direction and sensitivity. No outcome-dependent replacement or new contrast was introduced.

\subsection{Limited-label recognition gains do not ensure native localization}
Table~\ref{tab:confirmation_internal} shows all four internal SCDD label budgets on the same 117-image confirmation cohort. LoRA has higher mean image AUROC than the adapted CNN at every budget. Positive-image Dice improves at 5\%, decreases at 10\% and 100\%, and differs little at 20\%. Pooled native AP favors the CNN at the three larger budgets. The 5\% Dice gain also accompanies increased normal-structure FPR, from 0.00112 to 0.00383. Thus the smallest mask budget does not identify an inspection system with uniformly improved discrimination, overlap and false-positive behavior. The 120 validation masks and upstream UCF selection labels remain additional supervision.

\subsection{Acquisition-held-source recognition and overlap separate}
Across all six held-source/budget conditions, LoRA has higher mean image AUROC than the adapted CNN, with positive directions in all eighteen fitted pairs. The conditional unadjusted AUROC interval contains zero for CSIR 20\%; the other five intervals lie above zero. These intervals remain part of a 6,212-comparison family and do not imply adjusted significance or independent-domain replication. The small CFVS stratum contains only fifteen positives and twelve negatives; perfect observed AUROC in both budgets does not establish population-perfect prediction.

Dice is lower for LoRA in four of the six conditions (Table~\ref{tab:confirmation_held_Dice}). CSIR 20\% retains lower Dice in all three fitted pairs despite higher AUROC in all three. Thresholded review decisions also differ: CSIR 20\% LoRA increases review from 0.695 to 0.801 and image FPR from 0.420 to 0.638. Matching acquisition strata, rather than pooling uncalibrated models across channels, is essential to these interpretations.

\subsection{Source operating points fail under restricted PVEL transfer}
The complete PVEL population analysis reuses the same once-scored 12,326-image pool. These are failures of portable source operating points in the restricted population, rather than evidence of a deployable high-recall detector.

\subsection{Native failures, calibration and secondary controls}
Figure~\ref{fig:confirmation_native} retains all 496 native-mask jobs in the fixed crack-area bins. High image recall can coincide with low overlap and frequent literal zero-Dice masks, especially for small annotated crack footprints. Zero overlap need not mean an entirely empty prediction. All-positive and all-negative summaries remain separate; negative-field mean pixel FPR is not substituted for normal-structure FPR. PVEL box annotations never enter mask-Dice panels.

Source-temperature diagnostics retain Brier score, negative log-likelihood and fixed-bin ECE for every original scored model/cohort pool. Improvements are not universal, and no target temperature is fitted. These whole-pool diagnostics use 117 SCDD and 12,326 PVEL images, rather than matching held-source strata or the 12,292-image primary PVEL population. The full 29-question readout separately preserves frozen-feature/classifier controls, input scale and pooling, larger encoders, stronger CNN rates, full supervised/semi-supervised ports, correlated ensembles, literal numerical sensitivities and post-adaptation reference heads. Benefits in one endpoint do not establish complete-system dominance. The stronger image-only CNN controls also remain informative: all twelve original LoRA-minus-additional-CNN AUROC comparisons on SCDD 117 and UCF 507 are positive, with positive directions in all thirty-six fitted pairs. Against the ResNet-50 control at learning rate $10^{-5}$, the SCDD difference is 0.014 [-0.034, 0.066], whereas the UCF difference is 0.073 [0.028, 0.134], with conditional unadjusted intervals. The higher source-validation ResNet-50 ranking therefore does not persist uniformly in these confirmation comparisons. These reused fits and cohorts do not count as twelve independent studies or isolate a backbone effect. The fixed spatial record additionally retains all 3,780 original maps in 216 local sheets; no outcome-selected example is substituted.

\section{Discussion}
The complete confirmation results retain the development pattern of disagreement between recognition and localization. Higher LoRA AUROC across all six held-source conditions coexists with lower mean Dice in four. Within matched UCF supervision, improvement in both recognition and Dice is substantial relative to the supervised local port, but the same fitted systems transfer with adverse Dice on SCDD. This combination supports a task- and population-specific assessment of complete systems, rather than a single foundation-model ranking.

Source-selected high-recall thresholds are particularly fragile under restricted PVEL transfer. High recall with high author-normal FPR and inconsistent box-point recovery does not provide a useful autonomous inspection policy. The fixed population sensitivities describe the consequences of prespecified integrity and annotation restrictions; they do not estimate field prevalence or repair a poorly transferred operating point. No target calibration, threshold adjustment or favorable example selection is used to remove these failures.

Normal-reference and fresh-head controls retain mixed effects. Source memory coverage, retrieval, decoder optimization, annotation extent and acquisition appearance remain competing explanations. Equal decoder parameter counts remove one difference but do not establish a matching-specific cause. Similarly, published-architecture and semi-supervised ports differ in optimization work and unlabelled exposure. Correlated teacher/ensemble views and deterministic predictor reuse do not create new training replications.

Several limitations constrain inference. Both UCF and SCDD development informed study-wide design; disjoint confirmation identities do not make either dataset wholly unseen to research selection. Pretraining corpora, objectives and HPO budgets prevent architecture-only attribution. Provided acquisition families do not verify module identity; image integrity screening does not exclude all crop overlaps or pretraining membership. PVEL author-normal specificity does not extend to every other defect, and box truth cannot validate segmentation. UCF source-file provenance remains unresolved. Label-stratified subsets and reused validation masks do not identify annotation labour savings. Finally, the large family of unadjusted conditional intervals does not support multiplicity-adjusted superiority claims.

\section{Conclusion}
DINOv3 adaptation can improve label-limited crack recognition and selected native-mask comparisons, while localization, review burden and transferred operating points remain separate constraints. Complete fixed-cohort results expose both gains and failures: consistent held-source AUROC directions, mixed Dice effects, a favorable matched UCF mask comparison and high restricted-PVEL false-positive rates. Inspection studies should report these endpoints together, retain weak seeds and unavailable annotations, and make supervision and optimization exposure explicit.

\section{Reproducibility and availability}
The owner-side record retains immutable protocols, the single registry, ordered data identities, source exposure, original failures/pauses, optimizer/RNG state, selected weights, predictions and raw histories. A registered rerun of the unchanged statistical workflow reproduced all 1,683 saved-job records and 6,212 contrasts exactly apart from generation time, without overwriting the original analysis. This establishes repeatability on the same host, environment, implementation and saved outcomes; it does not establish independent-implementation, cross-device or fresh-training reproduction. The authorized-input package retains the exact four-author-file acquisition recipe and mandatory PV-S3 oracle check, while unknown-licensed upstream source remains excluded from distributable materials. The owner-only dependency index binds every saved prediction product and original cache-retirement receipt. Retired per-image AP intermediates remain distinguished from preserved final native summaries, predictions and fixed maps.

Data and model permissions are artifact-specific. ELPV image and code terms differ; PVEL repository and dataset-form conditions remain separate; absence of an explicit raw-data license in an inspected SCDD/UCF tree is not a blanket redistribution permission. DINOv3 and copied MIT-licensed PS-MT material retain their source attribution and applicable terms. Raw EL pixels/masks, prediction arrays and model/optimizer payloads are excluded from the sanitized private handoff. No public release or external submission is made here.

\begin{center}{\Large\bfseries Supplementary methods and complete confirmation controls}\end{center}
This supplement accompanies the completed single-registry confirmation analysis. It reports the original methods, all 29 overlapping control-question themes and all 456 endpoint comparisons in the six fixed dense-control table scopes. Complete machine-readable companions retain all 6,212 declarations and 16,140 fitted-pair records, including the other controls, original intervals, population sensitivities and unsupported per-job endpoints. No new model, contrast, calibration, population or example is introduced here. Direction counts describe overlapping comparisons, not independent wins or multiplicity-adjusted tests.

\section{Detailed source methods and exposure}
The main article distinguishes gradient-fit labels, validation labels and upstream hyperparameter exposure. The 18 masks at the smallest SCDD training budget require 120 additional validation masks, plus upstream UCF calibration. Matched UCF20\% fits use 86 training and 144 validation masks within the same 574-image HPO pool. Pretraining membership is unknown. These budgets describe available annotations, not measured annotation labour.

\subsection{Global frozen representations and image-only adaptation}
Whole grayscale images are copied into three channels, resized with bicubic letterboxing and normalized with the corresponding ImageNet convention. Input size is initially $336\times336$; enlarging an image does not recover absent physical detail. DINOv3-S/16 provides a 384-dimensional CLS vector and patch vectors. Register tokens are excluded from patch pooling. Image classifiers receive a per-image, non-affine layer-normalized vector.

The six primary image systems are DINOv3-S frozen, LoRA and full fine-tuning; and fully fine-tuned ResNet-18, ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-B0. Their final image heads are linear. LoRA uses rank 8, scaling 8 and query/value projections in the last four transformer blocks. It changes encoder projections; it is not an operation applied only to a stored embedding vector. CNN pretrained batch-normalization statistics remain fixed, with affine parameters trainable. Different pretraining data prevent a causal Transformer-versus-CNN interpretation.

Source-only calibration evaluates two learning rates per family and three paired seeds on UCF430/144. Primary real-cohort development contains 180 fits: 72 internal budget fits plus 108 acquisition-source-held-out fits at 20\% and 100\% source-training labels. Batches use synchronized whole-field D4 views, 50 updates per round, at most 40 rounds, AdamW~\cite{adamw} and source-validation AUROC early stopping with patience six. Source validation selects temperature and a high-recall decision threshold; no target threshold is fitted.

Converged Logistic Regression, Linear SVM and RBF SVM controls use HOG plus 42 intensity/gradient statistics (1,806 dimensions) or frozen CLS features. A separate 379-fit representation study compares CLS, image-area-weighted patch means and concatenation; DINOv3-S at 224/336/448; DINOv3-B at 336; and frozen ResNet-18 classifier probes. Full-budget deterministic probes are stored once. Classical and neural search grids have different sizes; equal tuning cost is not claimed.

\subsection{Matched dense networks and local normal structure}
An adapted DeepLabv3+/ResNet-50 baseline and a four-depth DINOv3 decoder share image and canonical pixel supervision. The DINO decoder reads transformer depths 3, 6, 9 and 12 and includes detail skips. Both use
\begin{equation}
\mathcal L=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{image\ BCE}}+\mathcal L_{\mathrm{weighted\ pixel\ CE}}+0.5\mathcal L_{\mathrm{crack\ Dice}}.
\end{equation}
Overlap-based training objectives have precedents including V-Net~\cite{vnet}. Our crack-class soft Dice term uses linear probability/indicator sums, additive-one smoothing and a per-image mean. V-Net uses squared denominator terms in its volumetric objective. The implemented loss combination is therefore specified here rather than presented as an exact V-Net reproduction.

Pixel class weights follow inverse square-root source frequencies. The source checkpoint metric uses up to 8,192 fixed, uniformly selected known transformed pixels per validation image; full native-mask metrics are reported at the selected checkpoint. Validation masks are charged as supervision.

Only selected training masks define normal references. At most 256 reference images are selected by frozen-CLS coverage; a query retrieves five similar images, then matches their eligible normal patches. The complete query capture family is excluded. For normalized patch vectors $q$ and $r$, matching minimizes
\begin{equation}
1-q^\top r+\lambda\lVert p_q-p_r\rVert_2^2,\qquad \lambda=0.1.
\end{equation}
The local network receives the query, query-minus-reference residual, coordinates and cosine distance. Its top 5\% local crack evidence is fused with global vectors for image classification. Reference-free, no-position and mean-evidence controls test the mechanism. The registered dense study has 24 UCF calibration and 144 real-cohort development fits; nine UCF-only reference fits preserve a source-only transfer comparison.

\subsection{Decoder dimensions and global/local fusion}
At a 336-pixel input, each projected transformer depth supplies a $21\times21\times128$ feature map. The normal-input slot concatenates normalized query features (384), matched residuals (384), coordinates (2) and cosine distance (1): 771 values project to 64 channels. The reference-free arm retains this same network, with residual and distance set to zero. Combining four depth projections and this slot gives 576 channels, fused to 128. Four grayscale-detail upsampling stages use widths 96, 64, 32 and 24 before the three-class output.

The frozen decoder/image head has 1,387,269 trainable parameters in both reference conditions. Rank-eight Q/V adapters in the last four blocks add 49,152 encoder parameters. Thus a reference comparison changes its input information while retaining decoder architecture and parameter count. The image head concatenates the final CLS and fully image-valid patch mean (768 features), applies non-affine LayerNorm, appends scalar top-five-percent local log-odds, and fits a 769-input linear output. Annotation-ignore regions remain visible in the image input; geometric image validity differs from pixel-loss eligibility.

\subsection{Explicit patch, distance and frozen post-LoRA controls}
A last-layer patch baseline uses a 128-hidden-unit MLP with three outputs. Patch targets max-preserve thin annotated cracks. Its image BCE, weighted patch CE and patch Dice objective differs from full-resolution segmentation, although the original annotated image identities are the same. Its upsampled map cannot supply arbitrary subpatch detail.

A normal-distance baseline compares query patches against at most 64 deterministically indexed normal patches per reference image/view. Nearest cosine distances are exact within that capped memory and exclude the query family. A source-validation noncrack response quantile fixes its pixel operating point. This mask-informed memory is not annotation-free; the resulting response is not a calibrated crack posterior. Native pixel AP is primary, and its cutoff convention is distinguished from learned softmax-score threshold 0.5.

For post-LoRA references, a source-trained adapter is merged into the original encoder, frozen and re-encoded before references are rebuilt. Two fresh decoder heads, with and without references, start identically and use exactly the parent's budgeted source images/masks. Their extra adaptation/head stages add computation, not new annotation identities. Each encoder export verifies merged and freshly reloaded tokens. Cache identities bind the actual merged weights. Exact canonical reference tensors persist; noncanonical D4 training intermediates are reproducible from source inputs and their recorded hashes. The mechanism study registers 36 patch fits/calibrations, 23 distance controls and 66 post-LoRA fresh-head fits. All 125 registered mechanism fits are complete; their complete source results and counterexamples remain in the separate source numerical companion and archived record.

\subsection{Comparison with published semi-supervised methods}
PV-S3~\cite{pvs3} and its acknowledged PS-MT basis~\cite{psmt} use teacher/student consistency, rather than the adapted supervised DeepLab baseline alone. We retain the complete MIT-licensed PS-MT deep-stem ResNet-50/DeepLabv3+ architecture, whose released encoder/decoder source matches the pinned PV-S3 architecture byte for byte. Each network has 41,762,595 parameters. The student uses the authors' publicly posted ImageNet initialization; EL-task-trained weights are not used because their overlap with confirmation images is unknown. Two teachers initialize independently, following the released role policy.

The implemented semi-supervised arm includes teacher-decoder virtual adversarial feature perturbation, confidence-weighted CE with positive threshold 0.6, weak/strong photometric views, CutMix with Beta(4,4), and EMA teacher updates with coefficient 0.996. The active teacher alternates by optimization round; after every student optimizer step, the active teacher for that round receives an EMA update. The student uses SGD with momentum 0.9, weight decay $10^{-4}$ and the registered polynomial learning-rate decay. All floating BN statistics and integer counters are saved. Supervision is pixel CE plus a ramped consistency loss, without the additional image BCE used by the DINO dense systems. Image scores aggregate the top 5\% crack-versus-other log-odds. Equal mask identities therefore do not imply identical training objectives or compute.

Weight-averaged teacher targets, adversarial prediction smoothness and rectangular image mixing build on Mean Teacher~\cite{meanteacher}, VAT~\cite{vat} and CutMix~\cite{cutmix}, respectively. Our port applies VAT in encoder-feature space through two frozen teacher decoders, and mixes spatial pseudo-logits and validity masks with image regions. Its Beta(4,4) setting differs from the original CutMix experiments' Beta(1,1). These are documented adaptations of component principles; original classification or medical-segmentation scores are not matched EL results.

The 69-fit protocol comprises 18 source hyperparameter fits, three fixed literal-VAT-setting sensitivity fits, 36 SCDD development fits, and 12 matched UCF20\% source fits. The supervised architecture uses 20\% and 100\% training masks; SSL uses 20\% plus the remaining source-training images without reading their masks. DINO frozen, LoRA and normal-reference source controls use the same 86 training masks and 144 validation masks. Full-source UCF and upstream dense hyperparameter calibration are additional annotation exposure, not hidden within the 20\% claim.

The port uses canonical three-class labels, whole-field 336-pixel letterboxing, batch two on MPS, synchronized D4 views and explicitly counted updates. These differ from the original five-class, crop-based experiment. The primary VAT finite-difference scale is 0.1, the released helper default. An initial local FP32 source-only precision probe found a substantially diminished perturbation with the released caller's scale $10^{-6}$; that literal setting remains a fixed three-seed source sensitivity. This diagnostic does not demonstrate failure of the authors' trained system on other hardware.

Primary inference uses teacher 1, matching released PV-S3 inference. A predeclared mean of both teacher logits, reflecting PS-MT paper inference, is evaluated at the identical source-selected checkpoint with its own source-calibrated operating point. It is a correlated inference view, not another trained seed or an option chosen using target scores. Exact FP32 parameters and complete normalization state are stored losslessly; full-resolution CPU forward/backward and fresh-model recovery checks passed with zero source-prediction error in the implementation probe. Those probe scores are excluded from research tables. All 18 source-calibration fits and the complete 69-fit full-method/matched-control schedule are complete and audited. These adaptations are not a reproduction of the published reported score.


\section{Endpoint definitions and complete reporting support}
Image decisions use the strict inequality $s_i>\tau_{\mathrm{source}}$ on the original saved score. Recall and FPR use annotated positive and negative image denominators; review is the fraction of all images flagged. AUROC and AP retain their different prevalence and ranking meanings. Source temperature is never fitted on target outcomes.

For known native pixels, the crack map uses the fixed strict score rule $p>0.5$; the source-calibrated distance system retains its model-specific response convention. With crack truth $G_i$ and predicted crack pixels $P_i$, Dice is $2|G_i\cap P_i|/(|G_i|+|P_i|)$ and IoU is $|G_i\cap P_i|/|G_i\cup P_i|$. Positive-image means exclude images without crack truth. All-image Dice, which can reward empty true-negative masks, does not replace positive-image overlap. Native pooled AP concatenates known pixels within each bounded SCDD/UCF cohort and is a whole-cohort point estimate. It is neither mean per-image AP nor an independent-pixel bootstrap.

SCDD normal-structure FPR pools false-positive pixels over annotated normal-structure pixels in crack-negative images only (the original raw annotation classes 4 and 9 after canonical eligibility). UCF lacks that annotation and remains null. A negative-field mean pixel FPR is a separate descriptive endpoint. PVEL box-point hit tests whether the maximum-response pixel centre falls in any target box, with the first row-major pixel resolving exact ties. It does not measure object-detection AP or mask Dice.

All 1,683 prediction jobs passed the original execution audit and the separate saved-output checks. The 630 spatial jobs comprise 496 SCDD/UCF native-mask jobs and 134 PVEL box jobs. Five fixed native-failure strata for each eligible job yield 2,480 records; 116 have empty denominators and retain null rates. The three positive bins are $(0,0.5\%]$, $(0.5\%,2\%]$ and above $2\%$ of known-pixel crack annotation. Zero overlap and detected-with-zero-overlap are literal events; a misplaced nonempty mask can have zero overlap. No physical crack severity is inferred from annotation area.

The 3,780 fixed display maps comprise 2,172 SCDD, 804 UCF and 804 PVEL maps, grouped into 216 local sheets. The original metadata-only cases are retained, including weak responses. These float16 display products do not replace full-precision metric summaries. Raw-image/mask redistribution is not inferred from local access.

All 311 PVEL views use the once-scored 12,326-image pool. The primary 12,292-image population, full pool and broader 11,927-image sensitivity are derived from the same saved scores; a line-only analysis additionally excludes star-crack positives under its fixed rule. The original 17 near-copy pairs and all 34 excluded members remain documented. Neither integrity screening nor these sensitivities establishes physical module identity, crop independence or pretraining exclusion. There is no PVEL capture-family confidence interval.

Calibration companions retain 5,049 model/cohort/metric rows for Brier score, negative log-likelihood and fixed-bin ECE. These diagnostics use the original whole pools of SCDD117, UCF507 and PVEL12,326, not the matching held-source strata or primary PVEL population. The four diagnostic sheets additionally preserve all native groups and all 3,732 population-sensitivity rows. Their descriptive points are correlated through fitted systems and image reuse.

\section{Interpretation of all original control questions}
Every Q-number below follows the order of the original pre-scoring question rationale. The trace table preserves each question's full FIRST/SECOND family IDs, cohort, stratum, endpoint, original mean and every fitted-pair difference. Question membership overlaps, so 6,252 memberships refer to 6,212 unique declarations. Each conditional interval remains unadjusted across this large family. Positive signed differences are not automatically beneficial, particularly for FPR and review burden.
\subsection{Q1: Adaptation across original image controls}
Most signed AUROC differences favor the original second-family image LoRA systems, but adverse and tied conditions remain. This does not establish a universally improved inspection operating point. Frozen features, full fine-tuning and CNN comparators have different pretraining and optimization histories; budgets and acquisition strata overlap.

\subsection{Q2: Frozen DINO and classical features with the same classifier}
The declared frozen-feature comparisons mostly have positive AUROC differences, with an adverse condition retained. The result concerns complete feature/preprocessing systems. Sharing a classifier does not match representation pretraining, dimensionality, preprocessing or annotation-dependent HPO.

\subsection{Q3: LoRA and classical controls}
All declared AUROC mean differences are positive in the original orientation. Thresholded review and transferred PVEL behavior require their own records. Neural adaptation and classical tuning have unequal search and optimization budgets; the comparisons do not isolate representation or training cost.

\subsection{Q4: Adaptation relative to frozen/classical predictors}
All declared AUROC mean differences are positive, conditional on these source-selected systems and fixed cohorts. The controls overlap the other image themes and are not independent confirmations of the same claim.

\subsection{Q5: Frozen representation systems}
Signed AUROC differences are predominantly positive but include an adverse comparison. Retain each original feature and processing recipe. Pretraining, geometry, dimensionality and pooling are confounded; an encoder architecture cause is not identified.

\subsection{Q6: Processing scale}
AUROC differences have both signs. Increasing processing scale is not uniformly beneficial across the declared source and target conditions. Resizing changes the complete input processing system; it does not recover missing physical information or establish a resolution mechanism.

\subsection{Q7: CLS and patch pooling}
Both signed AUROC directions occur; pooling effects depend on processing size and source condition. CLS, patch mean and concatenation differ in feature geometry and dimensionality. No pooling is selected from confirmation outcomes.

\subsection{Q8: Frozen larger encoder}
The original larger-encoder comparisons have positive AUROC differences, while positive PVEL recall changes accompany positive author-normal FPR changes. Larger models and pretraining differ. Recall alone does not establish improved operating decisions or resource efficiency.

\subsection{Q9: Model scale}
Both signed AUROC directions occur, although positive means are more frequent. The full original model-scale conditions remain separate. Parameter count and pretraining are not isolated causes; shared fitted systems and cohorts are correlated.

\subsection{Q10: ResNet and DINO with a common classifier}
All declared AUROC mean differences are positive in the original orientation. ImageNet and DINO pretraining differ. This is a complete frozen-feature comparison, not a randomized architecture comparison.

\subsection{Q11: Dense adaptation and original same-mask controls}
AUROC differences are mostly positive, whereas native Dice has nearly balanced positive and adverse means. Image ranking and native overlap do not provide interchangeable evidence. Same masks do not match pretraining, losses, optimization or source model selection. Keep all fitted-pair directions and pooled-AP point estimates.

\subsection{Q12: Normal reference relative to frozen dense prediction}
AUROC and Dice contain positive and adverse conditions; positive native-AP means do not imply uniform positive-image overlap or review improvements. Memory coverage, retrieval, decoder fitting and source annotation structure remain alternative explanations; no matching-specific cause is established.

\subsection{Q13: Local patch objective and decoder}
AUROC and Dice both have mixed signed differences. Changing objective and decoder does not produce an endpoint-uniform gain. These are complete systems with different supervision pathways and decoder structure, despite matching original annotation IDs where verified.

\subsection{Q14: Adapted multidepth and local patch systems}
The frozen declaration is adapted multidepth LoRA FIRST and patch MLP SECOND. All fourteen AUROC differences are negative; eleven of fourteen Dice mean differences are negative. The direction must not be reversed to match the prose label. Encoder adaptation, feature depth and decoder objectives change together.

\subsection{Q15: Source-calibrated normal distance}
The original normal-distance SECOND comparisons have adverse AUROC and native-AP differences and often larger normal-structure FPR. Their complete source cutoff is retained. A source normal-distance cutoff is not softmax 0.5 or a crack posterior. Matching and supervised decoder changes cannot be separated.

\subsection{Q16: Fresh decoder after encoder adaptation}
Fresh-head AUROC and Dice means include positive, adverse and tied behavior; extra head optimization can change the complete system. Fresh decoder initialization, encoder freezing and prior adaptation are jointly changed; parent work must be charged separately.

\subsection{Q17: Reference within matched fresh decoders}
Reference versus no-reference fresh heads have both signed AUROC and Dice differences, including ties. There is no uniform reference benefit. Same trainable count removes one difference but does not identify a unique retrieval mechanism or erase seed sensitivity.

\subsection{Q18: Full post-adaptation system and original parent}
Both positive and adverse AUROC and Dice effects remain, while native AP includes adverse means. Parent and new decoder stages are distinct fitted components. Additional optimization and changed encoder/decoder roles preclude a reference-only causal interpretation.

\subsection{Q19: Full supervised local published-architecture controls}
Many original SECOND dense-comparator means improve AUROC and Dice, while native AP retains numerous adverse conditions. The matched UCF LoRA gain transfers with lower mean SCDD Dice. Published-port objectives, pretraining and optimization work differ. These are local ports, not reproductions or rankings of published headline metrics.

\subsection{Q20: Semi-supervised and supervised local ports}
AUROC has both signed directions and Dice includes adverse and tied means. Unlabelled exposure does not guarantee a native-overlap benefit. The semi-supervised objective and unlabelled images are additional inputs. Teacher views share fitted weights and do not create independent training replications.

\subsection{Q21: Dense controls and semi-supervised local ports}
All declared AUROC means are positive in the original orientation, but native AP has more adverse than positive means. Dice and operating decisions need their own original records. Source-selected semi-supervised systems, primary teacher and ensemble are correlated; pretraining and optimizer work differ.

\subsection{Q22: Teacher ensemble}
Original teacher-ensemble differences have both AUROC directions and positive, adverse or tied Dice. Ensembling is not uniformly beneficial. The views share training. Their differences describe inference choices frozen before scoring, not independent fitted-model replications.

\subsection{Q23: Geometry and local evidence aggregation}
Position and top-5\%-versus-mean controls have mixed AUROC and Dice differences. No geometry or pooling setting is selected after scoring. The frozen controls differ in explicit geometry or aggregation; small cohorts and fitted-seed sensitivity limit mechanistic inference.

\subsection{Q24: Stronger image CNN optimization controls}
All twelve original LoRA-minus-additional-CNN AUROC means and all thirty-six fitted-pair directions are positive; the strongest ResNet-50 SCDD interval still includes zero. The CNN rates were post-hoc source sensitivities but fixed before confirmation. These reused fits and two cohorts are not twelve independent studies or an architecture effect.

\subsection{Q25: Literal numerical port sensitivity}
All four original SECOND literal-recipe AUROC, Dice and native-AP mean differences are negative. The selected-port and literal-port failures remain visible. The complete numerical recipe changes more than xi; this is not an xi-only causal test. No target-driven repair is made.

\subsection{Q26: Literal-port correlated ensemble}
The two AUROC differences have opposite directions, while both Dice means increase. The ensemble and teacher share fitting and the literal numerical recipe. Positive Dice does not imply a general ensemble benefit.

\subsection{Q27: Matched UCF20\% DINO controls}
Frozen-to-LoRA and reference-to-LoRA AUROC and Dice means are positive in both SCDD117 and UCF507. These four DINO contrasts do not denote the supervised-port comparison. The 86 training and 144 validation masks are nested within 574 development/HPO images; matched labels do not match pretraining, HPO or optimization.

\subsection{Q28: Matched UCF20\% normal reference}
Both original frozen-to-reference AUROC and Dice mean differences are negative on SCDD117 and UCF507. This is evidence against a universal reference benefit in these fits, not proof that reference information cannot help under other fixed systems.

\subsection{Q29: Original UCF-only reference transfer}
AUROC, Dice and native AP each retain positive and adverse future-transfer conditions. Source-only fitted weights do not make the target dataset unseen to research selection. Both datasets informed study-wide design, and transfer remains conditional on source-selected systems.

\section{Source context, computational cost and the separate ELPV supplement}
All original source schedules completed: 36 neural calibration and 180 development fits; 70 classical calibration and 180 development records; 168 dense fits; nine UCF-reference fits; 18 stronger-CNN stability fits; 379 representation records; and 125 mechanism records. The complete published-method schedule contains 69 audited source/matched fits, including 60 full-architecture and nine matched DINO fits. These counts refer to different catalogue stages, shared views and deterministic reuse; they are not a sum of independent architectures or all upstream HPO work.

The original full-budget internal dense source comparison has LoRA Dice 0.149 versus adapted CNN 0.198 despite higher image AUROC. The stronger source image-only ResNet-50 AUROC of 0.969 exceeds image-only LoRA 0.956. Matched UCF20\% source LoRA Dice is 0.404889 versus 0.307231 for the full supervised local port, with favorable directions in all three fits, while native AP and review behavior are not uniformly better. These source observations preceded confirmation and remain distinguished from the main article's actual confirmation values.

Formal efficiency covers 97 fitted cases, 388 cohort/batch conditions and 1,164 measured whole-cohort passes on the 32 GiB M2 Max. It uses 351 SCDD and 430 UCF source-training images, batches one and eight, warm-ups and three uninstrumented measured passes, with separate instrumentation and loading observations. Full-budget dense LoRA averages 31.73 ms/image on SCDD at batch one versus CNN 27.08, with mixed fitted-pair directions. RSS lifetime highwater and sampled MPS allocations overlap and are never added. These 97 cases do not independently time every final checkpoint.

The ELPV supplement uses only 1,968 course-development images and four grouped outer folds. Its 24 completed outer fits follow 480 inner-grid fits, with fold-specific scaling and parameter selection. Frozen DINOv3 CLS plus RBF SVM has mean outer AUROC 0.904918 versus 0.838261 for HOG/statistics plus RBF SVM; all four fold differences are positive. Overlapping training folds and expert-review labels prevent treating this as independent crack confirmation, a CNN comparison or a training-population interval. The 656 course-test images remain unscored. All six systems, eight endpoints and fold values remain in the fourteen-page vector source/cost/ELPV numerical companion.

\section{Reproduction boundaries, provenance and retained failures}
The owner-side records bind 26,259 authorized original inputs and a completed output closure of 11,142 saved job files, including 1,683 result/prediction pairs, 3,780 fixed maps and 630 original cache-retirement receipts. Full inventories and image identities are owner-only. The frozen scientific closure contains 92 exact files and one already observed registry. A separately authorized reproduction must satisfy the original path and byte guards; missing inputs cannot be replaced with symlinks, random weights, fabricated labels or skipped oracles.

The code package retains the sibling research/course code layout, dependency pins, model initialization and local-port provenance. The exact four-author-file recipe specifies the original PS-MT encoder, ResNet implementation, MIT notice and PV-S3 loss oracle by pinned source and hash. Upstream PV-S3 oracle source has no verified redistribution licence and is excluded from the transferable code-only package; an authorized recipient must review terms and obtain those exact inputs. The PV-S3 numerical oracle check remains mandatory and must fail explicitly when its inputs are absent. The owner's completed acquisition probe does not grant redistribution rights.

Historical implementation evidence consists of 171 original-environment and 164 separate fresh-environment checks with 53 pins on the same host/base Python. These are synthetic, metadata and numerical-oracle checks, not OS isolation, cross-device determinism, fresh-training performance reproduction or tests of every later reporting script. Complete saved-output auditing and the separately registered same-host statistical replay have separate evidence and scope. The replay completed successfully and reproduced every saved-job and declared contrast field apart from generation time; the original analysis bytes remained unchanged. This is same-host, same-environment, same-implementation repeatability on the same saved outputs, not independent-implementation, cross-device, OS-isolation or fresh-training reproduction.

Original training and reporting failures remain append-only. The zero-extra-update recovery retains its original 19-round/950-step fit, optimizer/RNG and selected weights. Three owner-pause-contaminated round/fit timers and a recovery-finalization timer remain raw; they are not silently converted to active compute. The candidate-inventory v1 seed-grouping failure and separate v2 grouping-only amendment retain all 1,061 original run/weight/threshold/source-output fields. Reporting-only JSON parsing, omitted output lists, ambiguous recipe labels and clipped single-panel figures have explicit retained originals and presentation supersession records. None changes the frozen evaluator, scientific populations, scores or choices.

Raw EL images, masks, labels, fitted/pretrained weights, optimizer/RNG payloads, prediction arrays and full owner input/output inventories are excluded from the sanitized private handoff. Dataset, model and code terms remain distinct. No public release, external submission or contact is performed. Author and venue fields remain intentionally deferred by the owner.

\section{Introduction and research questions}
Electroluminescence (EL) images reveal spatial structures associated with photovoltaic defects. Image-level review decisions and pixel-level crack localization are related tasks, but they require different ground truth. Deitsch et al.~\cite{deitsch} compare handcrafted-feature SVM and CNN approaches for ELPV. Fioresi et al.~\cite{fioresi} study semantic defect segmentation. These reported scores cannot be ranked against a new crack AUROC without matching the cohort, labels and evaluation protocol.

A strong pretrained encoder can reduce the parameters fitted to a small EL dataset. However, a high validation AUROC does not establish reliable operation on another acquisition source. It can also conceal missed thin cracks or false responses to normal structures. We therefore ask: (i) how do frozen, low-rank and full adaptation differ under limited labels and acquisition shift; (ii) does local evidence help beyond a global image vector; and (iii) do normal-structure references improve localization and source-frozen operating decisions when given the same original mask annotations?

The normal-reference hypothesis is conditional. If it does not improve the matched local baseline consistently, it will be reported as a negative result. Existing industrial DINOv3 transfer research~\cite{gharbage} and EL cross-domain work prevent a broad novelty claim based only on applying a foundation model.

\section{Related methods and scope of comparison}
HOG~\cite{hog} and support-vector classification~\cite{svm} motivate the handcrafted and frozen-feature controls. ResNet~\cite{resnet} and EfficientNet~\cite{efficientnet} supply convolutional baselines; DeepLabv3+~\cite{deeplab} supplies the segmentation architecture family. Our HOG/statistics fusion, modified task heads and adapted PS-MT architecture are specified separately. The original method papers establish attribution, not EL performance in our cohort. LoRA~\cite{lora} parametrizes weight changes with low-rank matrices while freezing the original weights. It changes the encoder, whereas a new classifier learns a mapping from its output. Its original language-model results do not establish a photovoltaic advantage. Temperature scaling~\cite{calibration} supplies source-fitted probability calibration, without guaranteeing calibration after acquisition shift.

Local nominal-feature comparison is established prior work. PatchCore~\cite{patchcore} combines intermediate pretrained CNN features, local aggregation, representative coreset memory and nearest-neighbor scoring. AnomalyDINO~\cite{anomalydino} uses frozen DINOv2 patch features, cosine-neighbor distances, reference rotations and optional feature-derived foreground masking. Its default image statistic averages the largest 1\% of patch distances. We review that paper as prior art; DINOv2 is not downloaded or executed in this study.

SuperADD~\cite{superadd} already combines DINOv3 with nominal-feature memory under acquisition variation. Its public workshop-challenge technical report describes a ViT-H+/16 backbone, four intermediate feature banks, overlapping 640-pixel processing windows, intensity augmentation, memory subsampling and morphological postprocessing. It is distinct from a CVPR main-conference publication. Consequently, neither DINOv3-based industrial transfer nor DINOv3 plus local normal memory is claimed as our invention.

Our registered experiment instead tests crack-specific, mask-informed normal references within supervised global/local prediction, with matched annotation identities and explicit source exposure. Its global retrieval, position-regularized residual input and learned decoder differ from the training-free pipelines above. A distance-only control is an adaptation of the nominal-neighbor principle, not an exact reproduction of PatchCore, AnomalyDINO or SuperADD. Other annotated defects are difficult crack-negative cases here but may be anomalies under those papers' tasks. Their MVTec/VisA scores therefore cannot rank against our EL scores. The intended contribution is the evidence on label requirements, native crack localization, source-frozen decisions and acquisition transfer, including failures. Existing PV-S3/PS-MT methods receive separately documented supervised and semi-supervised comparisons under our task protocol; no published headline score is presented as a matched result.

\section{Data, labels and exposure audit}
\subsection{Primary SCDD cohort}
We retain 588 audited real images from the ARTS, CFVS and CSIR acquisition channels in the public SCDD release. Reused public-source channels, augmentation aliases, exact rotation/reflection duplicates and ambiguous crack-negative records are handled before splitting. The primary split contains 351 training, 120 validation and 117 sealed test images (156, 54 and 53 crack positives, respectively). The 471 development images are reused to define source-held-out development; no independently confirmed test result is reported here.

Provided capture-family prefixes are conservative grouping units. They are not verified physical module identities. The whole field of view is retained, including neighboring cell regions where present. A positive image means an explicit crack annotation anywhere in that field of view, not measured central-cell power loss or electrical failure.

The release ontology maps indices 10 and 14 to crack; indices 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 9 and 24 to the canonical normal category; and the specified remaining intrinsic defects to other defect. Border, text, padding, clamp, frame edge, junction-box and measurement-artifact labels are excluded from the canonical pixel task. Ambiguous star-only negatives are not treated as reliable crack negatives. An ignored pixel therefore need not lack annotation: it can be a deliberately excluded annotated region. Negative means no explicitly annotated crack, rather than physically healthy.

\subsection{UCF source development and supplemental confirmation}
The observed UCF source cohort contains 430 training and 144 validation images. Their image labels select image-model hyperparameters; their masks additionally support the dense studies. The source paper includes simulated training images~\cite{fioresi}, but per-file provenance of the available source subset has not been established. We therefore do not describe this UCF cohort as individually verified real-only data.

A separate 507-image candidate confirmation cohort is group-disjoint from the 574 observed source images, with 181 crack positives. It follows the authors' reported test-real policy, subject to that provenance limitation. Missing/unknown annotation is not converted automatically into a negative label; raw UCF index 128 remains ignored. The released official train and test directories do not by themselves prove capture-family independence.

UCF development labels select hyperparameters later used by SCDD-fitted models. Consequently, SCDD-to-UCF507 is sample-disjoint confirmation in a development-exposed dataset, not a wholly unseen-dataset selection experiment. We preserve UCF-only source-fitted systems as a separate transfer direction and record both gradient-fit, unlabelled image and upstream hyperparameter-selection identities.

The research process also inspects SCDD development outcomes when choosing methodological follow-ups. This study-wide method-design exposure differs from the gradient, checkpoint and hyperparameter exposure of an individual UCF-only model. Its fixed-weight transfer to SCDD provides group-disjoint predictions on a dataset already studied during method development; the research process cannot call SCDD wholly unseen. During source-method design, PVEL predictive outcomes remained unopened, while its raw images and ontology had been audited. Scoring began only after the single final registry was frozen.

\subsection{Restricted PVEL-AD and ELPV scope}
Before the additional near-copy analysis policy below, the authorized PVEL-AD confirmation pool contains 977 explicitly annotated crack/star-crack positives and 11,349 author-normal images. Other-defect images with uncertain crack-negative completeness and official-test images without XML are excluded from reliable-negative claims. Primary readouts will be known-crack sensitivity and author-normal false-positive rate. Its constructed class mixture is not an estimate of operational prevalence. Box point localization is a coarse diagnostic, not pixel AP or detection mAP. Physical capture groups are unavailable, so no physical-module bootstrap interval is assigned.

The earlier ELPV course task uses an expert review label, not a crack mask. Its results remain separate, and its 656-image course test set is unopened. The present paper does not reinterpret ELPV expert certainty as physical damage severity.

\subsection{Whole-frame integrity review before model confirmation}
A nonlearned whole-frame audit covers 15,963 source, candidate-confirmation and ELPV-development images. A D4-aware 64-pixel perceptual-hash/correlation screen examines 4,830 candidate pairs; 238 pass the screen and 18 pass stricter 128-pixel correlation/high-pass criteria. The screening thresholds precede model confirmation. Native-resolution review retains all diagnostic sheets. Seventeen strong pairs are within the PVEL candidate pool, and one is within observed SCDD training. Three weaker SCDD source-to-confirmation candidates show different printed module identifiers and native structures; visual grid similarity alone does not justify their removal.

All 17 reviewed PVEL pairs have differing target boxes. Fifteen show matching detailed structure with noise-like residuals, and two are almost pixel-identical. These observations support conservative near-copy quarantine, not a verified generator, recapture history or physical-module identity. Before model scoring, we freeze a primary view excluding all 34 PVEL pair members and retain both the full authorized pool and a broader screen-exclusion sensitivity (Table~\ref{tab:population}).

\subsection{Annotation availability and annotation conventions}
The internal budgets are 5\%, 10\%, 20\% and 100\% of the 351-image training pool: 18, 36, 70 and 351 training images, with the same 120 validation labels additional. Subsets are nested and class-stratified within each seed. This simulates label availability; class-stratification itself uses the audited labels and is not a prospective annotation-acquisition experiment. It does not establish an 80\% or 95\% saving in annotation time. Pixel masks and image labels are reported as different supervision, with UCF calibration exposure counted separately.

The SCDD paper explicitly contrasts narrow masks with broader regions in earlier UCF work~\cite{pratt}. Cross-dataset pixel scores may therefore reflect annotation extent as well as acquisition and population differences. The current data do not identify their separate causal effects. Same-policy SCDD source-held-out test strata are planned for localization confirmation.

\subsection{Native annotation support and metric weighting}
A retrospective audit uses the original native known/crack pixel counts in saved source-validation summaries. The annotation identities and counts agree across all included matched model/seed evaluations of each cohort. Those repeated outputs are checks of the same annotations, not independent annotation replications. The two cohorts contain 144 UCF and 120 SCDD images. Canonical task-ignored pixels are excluded from the denominator.
