The cohorts have 754,371 and 72,126 annotated crack pixels, respectively. In SCDD, CFVS contributes 59.3\% of positive images but 86.7\% of annotated crack pixels. ARTS contributes 14.8\% of positive images and 1.4\% of crack pixels; CSIR contributes 25.9\% and 11.8\%, respectively. The six largest positive SCDD masks account for 62.8\% of its annotated crack pixels, compared with 33.5\% for the six largest UCF masks.
This observed support distribution motivates reporting both pooled native pixel AP and equally weighted positive-image Dice. Positive-pixel shares do not decompose AP, which also depends on score ordering and noncrack pixels. The counts do not measure physical crack size, electrical severity or annotation time, and do not isolate annotation conventions from acquisition/content. Different source fits, labels and pixel prevalences prevent ranking the two cohorts' AP values as the same experiment.


\section{Methods and registered controls}
\subsection{Global frozen representations and image-only adaptation}
Whole grayscale images are copied into three channels, resized with bicubic letterboxing and normalized with the corresponding ImageNet convention. Input size is initially $336\times336$; enlarging an image does not recover absent physical detail. DINOv3-S/16 provides a 384-dimensional CLS vector and patch vectors. Register tokens are excluded from patch pooling. Image classifiers receive a per-image, non-affine layer-normalized vector.

The six primary image systems are DINOv3-S frozen, LoRA and full fine-tuning; and fully fine-tuned ResNet-18, ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-B0. Their final image heads are linear. LoRA uses rank 8, scaling 8 and query/value projections in the last four transformer blocks. It changes encoder projections; it is not an operation applied only to a stored embedding vector. CNN pretrained batch-normalization statistics remain fixed, with affine parameters trainable. Different pretraining data prevent a causal Transformer-versus-CNN interpretation.

Source-only calibration evaluates two learning rates per family and three paired seeds on UCF430/144. Primary real-cohort development contains 180 fits: 72 internal budget fits plus 108 acquisition-source-held-out fits at 20\% and 100\% source-training labels. Batches use synchronized whole-field D4 views, 50 updates per round, at most 40 rounds, AdamW~\cite{adamw} and source-validation AUROC early stopping with patience six. Source validation selects temperature and a high-recall decision threshold; no target threshold is fitted.

Converged Logistic Regression, Linear SVM and RBF SVM controls use HOG plus 42 intensity/gradient statistics (1,806 dimensions) or frozen CLS features. A separate 379-fit representation study compares CLS, image-area-weighted patch means and concatenation; DINOv3-S at 224/336/448; DINOv3-B at 336; and frozen ResNet-18 classifier probes. Full-budget deterministic probes are stored once. Classical and neural search grids have different sizes; equal tuning cost is not claimed.

\subsection{Matched dense networks and local normal structure}
An adapted DeepLabv3+/ResNet-50 baseline and a four-depth DINOv3 decoder share image and canonical pixel supervision. The DINO decoder reads transformer depths 3, 6, 9 and 12 and includes detail skips. Both use
\begin{equation}
\mathcal L=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{image\ BCE}}+\mathcal L_{\mathrm{weighted\ pixel\ CE}}+0.5\mathcal L_{\mathrm{crack\ Dice}}.
\end{equation}
Overlap-based training objectives have precedents including V-Net~\cite{vnet}. Our crack-class soft Dice term uses linear probability/indicator sums, additive-one smoothing and a per-image mean. V-Net uses squared denominator terms in its volumetric objective. The implemented loss combination is therefore specified here rather than presented as an exact V-Net reproduction.

Pixel class weights follow inverse square-root source frequencies. The source checkpoint metric uses up to 8,192 fixed, uniformly selected known transformed pixels per validation image; full native-mask metrics are reported at the selected checkpoint. Validation masks are charged as supervision.

Only selected training masks define normal references. At most 256 reference images are selected by frozen-CLS coverage; a query retrieves five similar images, then matches their eligible normal patches. The complete query capture family is excluded. For normalized patch vectors $q$ and $r$, matching minimizes
\begin{equation}
1-q^\top r+\lambda\lVert p_q-p_r\rVert_2^2,\qquad \lambda=0.1.
\end{equation}
The local network receives the query, query-minus-reference residual, coordinates and cosine distance. Its top 5\% local crack evidence is fused with global vectors for image classification. Reference-free, no-position and mean-evidence controls test the mechanism. The registered dense study has 24 UCF calibration and 144 real-cohort development fits; nine UCF-only reference fits preserve a source-only transfer comparison.

\subsection{Decoder dimensions and global/local fusion}
At a 336-pixel input, each projected transformer depth supplies a $21\times21\times128$ feature map. The normal-input slot concatenates normalized query features (384), matched residuals (384), coordinates (2) and cosine distance (1): 771 values project to 64 channels. The reference-free arm retains this same network, with residual and distance set to zero. Combining four depth projections and this slot gives 576 channels, fused to 128. Four grayscale-detail upsampling stages use widths 96, 64, 32 and 24 before the three-class output.

The frozen decoder/image head has 1,387,269 trainable parameters in both reference conditions. Rank-eight Q/V adapters in the last four blocks add 49,152 encoder parameters. Thus a reference comparison changes its input information while retaining decoder architecture and parameter count. The image head concatenates the final CLS and fully image-valid patch mean (768 features), applies non-affine LayerNorm, appends scalar top-five-percent local log-odds, and fits a 769-input linear output. Annotation-ignore regions remain visible in the image input; geometric image validity differs from pixel-loss eligibility.

\subsection{Explicit patch, distance and frozen post-LoRA controls}
A last-layer patch baseline uses a 128-hidden-unit MLP with three outputs. Patch targets max-preserve thin annotated cracks. Its image BCE, weighted patch CE and patch Dice objective differs from full-resolution segmentation, although the original annotated image identities are the same. Its upsampled map cannot supply arbitrary subpatch detail.

A normal-distance baseline compares query patches against at most 64 deterministically indexed normal patches per reference image/view. Nearest cosine distances are exact within that capped memory and exclude the query family. A source-validation noncrack response quantile fixes its pixel operating point. This mask-informed memory is not annotation-free; the resulting response is not a calibrated crack posterior. Native pixel AP is primary, and its cutoff convention is distinguished from learned softmax-score threshold 0.5.

For post-LoRA references, a source-trained adapter is merged into the original encoder, frozen and re-encoded before references are rebuilt. Two fresh decoder heads, with and without references, start identically and use exactly the parent's budgeted source images/masks. Their extra adaptation/head stages add computation, not new annotation identities. Each encoder export verifies merged and freshly reloaded tokens. Cache identities bind the actual merged weights. Exact canonical reference tensors persist; noncanonical D4 training intermediates are reproducible from source inputs and their recorded hashes. The mechanism study registers 36 patch fits/calibrations, 23 distance controls and 66 post-LoRA fresh-head fits. All 125 registered mechanism fits are complete; their source results and counterexamples are reported below.

\subsection{Comparison with published semi-supervised methods}
PV-S3~\cite{pvs3} and its acknowledged PS-MT basis~\cite{psmt} use teacher/student consistency, rather than the adapted supervised DeepLab baseline alone. We retain the complete MIT-licensed PS-MT deep-stem ResNet-50/DeepLabv3+ architecture, whose released encoder/decoder source matches the pinned PV-S3 architecture byte for byte. Each network has 41,762,595 parameters. The student uses the authors' publicly posted ImageNet initialization; EL-task-trained weights are not used because their overlap with confirmation images is unknown. Two teachers initialize independently, following the released role policy.

The implemented semi-supervised arm includes teacher-decoder virtual adversarial feature perturbation, confidence-weighted CE with positive threshold 0.6, weak/strong photometric views, CutMix with Beta(4,4), and EMA teacher updates with coefficient 0.996. The active teacher alternates by optimization round; after every student optimizer step, the active teacher for that round receives an EMA update. The student uses SGD with momentum 0.9, weight decay $10^{-4}$ and the registered polynomial learning-rate decay. All floating BN statistics and integer counters are saved. Supervision is pixel CE plus a ramped consistency loss, without the additional image BCE used by the DINO dense systems. Image scores aggregate the top 5\% crack-versus-other log-odds. Equal mask identities therefore do not imply identical training objectives or compute.

Weight-averaged teacher targets, adversarial prediction smoothness and rectangular image mixing build on Mean Teacher~\cite{meanteacher}, VAT~\cite{vat} and CutMix~\cite{cutmix}, respectively. Our port applies VAT in encoder-feature space through two frozen teacher decoders, and mixes spatial pseudo-logits and validity masks with image regions. Its Beta(4,4) setting differs from the original CutMix experiments' Beta(1,1). These are documented adaptations of component principles; original classification or medical-segmentation scores are not matched EL results.

The 69-fit protocol comprises 18 source hyperparameter fits, three fixed literal-VAT-setting sensitivity fits, 36 SCDD development fits, and 12 matched UCF20\% source fits. The supervised architecture uses 20\% and 100\% training masks; SSL uses 20\% plus the remaining source-training images without reading their masks. DINO frozen, LoRA and normal-reference source controls use the same 86 training masks and 144 validation masks. Full-source UCF and upstream dense hyperparameter calibration are additional annotation exposure, not hidden within the 20\% claim.

The port uses canonical three-class labels, whole-field 336-pixel letterboxing, batch two on MPS, synchronized D4 views and explicitly counted updates. These differ from the original five-class, crop-based experiment. The primary VAT finite-difference scale is 0.1, the released helper default. An initial local FP32 source-only precision probe found a substantially diminished perturbation with the released caller's scale $10^{-6}$; that literal setting remains a fixed three-seed source sensitivity. This diagnostic does not demonstrate failure of the authors' trained system on other hardware.

Primary inference uses teacher 1, matching released PV-S3 inference. A predeclared mean of both teacher logits, reflecting PS-MT paper inference, is evaluated at the identical source-selected checkpoint with its own source-calibrated operating point. It is a correlated inference view, not another trained seed or an option chosen using target scores. Exact FP32 parameters and complete normalization state are stored losslessly; full-resolution CPU forward/backward and fresh-model recovery checks passed with zero source-prediction error in the implementation probe. Those probe scores are excluded from research tables. All 18 source-calibration fits and the complete 69-fit full-method/matched-control schedule are complete and audited. These adaptations are not a reproduction of the published reported score.

\subsection{End-to-end inference efficiency}
The registered benchmark covers 97 fitted model/seed/inference-view cases, including 15 additional 20\%-budget normal-reference/distance cases because memory size depends on annotation availability. Every case processes the same 351 observed SCDD and 430 observed UCF source-training images, with no labels or masks supplied to the scorer. Batch sizes 1 and 8 each use five warm-up batches, partial-batch warm-up and three full-cohort measured passes. Separate processes and released training locks prevent overlap with our own training jobs. The actual host is an Apple M2 Max with 32 GiB unified memory.

Primary latency includes image checksum/read/decode, preprocessing, model encoding, reference matching where used, transfers, source-calibrated decisions and native-map reconstruction. Loading is measured separately. A separate synchronized instrumentation pass reports components; it does not replace uninstrumented latency. Kernel RSS highwater includes loading, and 10 ms sampled MPS tensor/driver maxima are observed allocations, not guaranteed peaks or CUDA VRAM. Unified-memory pools overlap. All logits and fixed native-pixel samples must agree across batching, repeated and instrumented passes. The complete-corpus verifier checks every job, input count, repetition and signature. All 97 formal cases are complete and verified; small CPU engineering probes are excluded from efficiency results. The single final-confirmation gate requires this benchmark to be complete.

\subsection{Supplementary ELPV review-label bridge}
The separate ELPV supplement preserves the original 1,968 course-development identities and four outer folds. Frozen DINOv3-S CLS vectors and the original 1,806-dimensional HOG/statistics cache each feed Logistic Regression, Linear SVM and RBF SVM. Three inner grouped folds select regularization, and RBF width where applicable, using outer-training labels only. Scaling is fitted within each training fold. This produces 24 outer-fold fits and 480 inner-grid fits. Default score zero supplies secondary decisions; no held-out threshold is fitted. These are exploratory expert-review labels, not crack annotations. The older course comparison used a different parameter-selection convention, so only the new matched nested controls are compared directly. The 656 course-test images remain unopened. Execution followed the complete source inference-cost benchmark; all 24 outer fits and the registered 480 inner-grid fits are now complete, with all outer saved outputs checked.

\subsection{Fresh-environment implementation verification}
A separate environment installs all 53 exact pinned dependencies from official PyPI, passes the package-consistency check and runs all 164 implementation checks from a hash-verified copied code/metadata tree. Python audit-hook guards deny the original site-packages, original research/course data, pretrained/auth caches and network access during the tests; no denied access was attempted. The copied source remains unchanged. The first new-environment installation succeeded, but its launcher omitted the copied project import path and blocked its own proof output. That failure is preserved; the amended launcher passes in a second separately installed environment.

These tests cover synthetic CPU training/evaluation fixtures, metadata guards and upstream numerical oracles. They use the same host and base Python, omit raw images, learned/pretrained weights and research prediction caches, and provide Python-level guards rather than operating-system isolation. They establish implementation installation consistency, not cross-device determinism or reproduction of research performance. The final research package still requires authorized inputs, fitted checkpoints, recorded predictions and the completed paper.

\section{Validation and statistical analysis}
Primary image readouts are AUROC, average precision (AP), macro-F1 and balanced accuracy, plus recall, false-positive rate and review fraction at a source-frozen operating point. AP uses the average-precision definition rather than trapezoidal integration of a precision--recall curve. Pixel AP, positive-image Dice/IoU and normal-structure false positives address localization; box-only data are kept separate. Small annotated crack area and normal-structure neighborhoods define failure analyses, without treating a heatmap as proof of physical understanding.

The existing plan resamples provided acquisition families in 1,000 paired bootstrap replicates and averages per-seed metric differences, rather than ensembling scores. Intervals are conditional on the three fitted seed models. Training-seed variability is reported separately. Development comparisons are exploratory and are not adjusted confirmatory significance tests. Patches are not independent experimental repetitions.

After all original source, full-method, formal-cost and ELPV gates completed, a new source review fixed one registry of models, source thresholds, code, runtime versions, data identities, upstream label exposure and endpoints (Section~\ref{sec:frozenactual}). Unknown crack negatives and exact-D4/provided-family overlap were rejected using the registered identity metadata. This does not prove absence of all cropped overlap, near-copies or pretraining membership. The actual registry is frozen and observed; neither it nor its scientific choices can be replaced after predictive access.

The minimum free-space policy is 16~GiB before each job; only owned derived pixel intermediates may be retired after complete saved-output identity/count/score checks. Raw inputs, best weights, predictions, native summaries and fixed example maps remain. A partial failure counts as observed and permits only exact frozen continuation, not replacement scientific choices.

Every declared job has now finished and passed the original complete saved-identity/logit/source-operating-point/calibration audit. No target model was fitted or operating point recalibrated by that audit. Every one of the 6,212 declared contrasts and each secondary native-failure stratum must be reported, including failures and non-estimable outcomes; no favorable post-score subset is selected. The article will separate the original adaptation, annotation, localization and source-transfer questions from the complete supplemental controls, without using target scores to choose a replacement model or hypothesis.

At 20\% masks, LoRA versus the full supervised port has higher mean image AUROC (0.936 versus 0.595) and positive-image Dice (0.160 versus 0.045), but lower native pixel AP (0.200 versus 0.254). Each of the three fitted pairs has these respective directions. The adapted supervised CNN is a different comparator: its 20\% Dice is 0.155, much closer to LoRA. At full masks, that adapted CNN has higher Dice than LoRA (0.198 versus 0.149), while the full supervised port again has higher pixel AP than LoRA (0.264 versus 0.224). These endpoint-dependent source findings do not establish a blanket advantage over CNNs.
Zero normal-structure pixel FPR in the full supervised port must be read together with its conservative native masks. At 20\%, 47, 44 and 48 of the 54 crack-positive images have entirely empty predictions at the fixed 0.5 pixel cutoff. At full masks those counts are 44, 41 and 48. The SSL teacher-1 view has 45, 43 and 49 empty positives at 20\%; its ensemble retains the same empty-positive counts. These counts and all other fitted models remain in the companion failure table. Zero structure-pixel errors therefore coexist with poor crack recovery. Meanwhile the supervised port flags more than 96\% of source-validation images at its separately calibrated image operating point. Low structure-pixel FPR is not low image-level review burden.
All systems have source recall approximately 0.963 because their image thresholds were selected on these same validation labels; this is not an independent sensitivity estimate. DINO and the adapted CNN use a learned image head and image BCE plus pixel CE/Dice, whereas the published architecture port uses pixel supervision and top-local-score image aggregation, with additional teacher consistency in SSL. Losses, score construction, pretraining and optimizer work differ. The observed image AUROC difference does not isolate a backbone or matching-specific cause, nor reproduce the authors\textquotesingle\ published numerical experiment.
The retrospective readout retains all 31 applicable paired contrasts, all six endpoints and all three fitted-seed differences, without new bootstrap intervals, p-values, thresholds or selected inference views. The source-validation reuse and annotation-subset variation remain explicit. Raw fit timers are provenance only: the internal 20\% SSL seed22 fit includes the later user pause, in addition to the separately documented earlier UCF seed33 pause. Neither affected raw duration is interpreted as active compute. All later source/cost/supplement schedules are now complete (Section~\ref{sec:completedgates}); confirmation prediction and its complete audit have finished under the single frozen registry; this readout remains source/development evidence while full statistics run.

Its mean positive-image Dice is lower (0.089 versus 0.103), with one favorable and two adverse fitted differences. Mean native pixel AP is higher (0.053 versus 0.042), but only one of the three fitted AP differences is favorable. The adapted CNN seed22 has empty predictions on all 45 positives, contributing to that mean comparison; its failure is retained alongside the other seeds. LoRA itself has 30, 17 and 23 empty positive masks across seeds11,22,33. A favorable image ranking or mean AP does not establish stable crack recovery.
At frozen source operating points, LoRA recall falls from approximately 0.971 on source validation to 0.763 on held ARTS; its held image review fraction is 0.442. The adapted CNN has held recall 0.630 and review fraction 0.598. These are different achieved sensitivities, with substantial fitted-seed variation, rather than a comparison at matched target recall. No target threshold is fitted to equalize or improve them.
The supervised port and both SSL inference views have empty predictions on every one of the 45 held positives for every seed, hence zero positive-image Dice. This does not mean every negative-image mask is empty: the supervised port has 150, 143 and 150 empty masks out of all151 images; SSL teacher-1 and ensemble each have 151,150,151. A few predicted crack pixels on negative images therefore coexist with zero eligible normal-structure pixel FPR. The structure subset, whole negative field, positive recovery and image operating point remain distinct endpoints.
SSL teacher-1 has higher held mean image AUROC than the supervised port (0.537 versus 0.363; all three fitted directions favorable), yet both have zero positive overlap and native AP near 0.003. The ensemble mean AUROC is 0.533; its AUROC and native AP differences from teacher-1 are adverse for all three held fitted pairs. Both views remain visible and are not independent fits. These results retain the specified local-port limitations and do not establish failure of the authors\textquotesingle\ original numerical experiments. No score-direction reversal, native-cutoff change or target calibration follows from the poor outcomes.
The original complete-cell identities, source-selected checkpoints, source thresholds/temperatures, all six endpoints and all fitted seeds are unchanged. This retrospective readout adds no model inference, bootstrap interval or significance claim. Both annotation budgets reuse the same observed acquisition cohort; pretraining, objectives, score construction, optimizer work and annotation/content differences remain confounds. All original source/cost/ELPV schedules are now complete; separately frozen final confirmation remains required (Section~\ref{sec:completedgates}).

Original score direction, source temperatures, source thresholds, checkpoints and native cutoffs are preserved. No new inference, bootstrap, target-driven selection or significance test is added. DINOv3 LoRA & 0.810 & 0.018 & 0.952 & 0.762\\
DINOv3 full & 0.762 & 0.029 & 0.905 & 0.667\\
\bottomrule\end{tabular}
\end{table}
The selected full-adaptation system combines pooled native pixel AP 0.736 with a mean zero-overlap fraction 0.905 in this small-footprint group. LoRA has a mean fraction 0.952 and the adapted CNN 0.619. These means do not create 21 independent small-crack images. All 58 positive-image points and every seed/group outcome remain available.

All four systems have mean image recall 0.966 over the 58 source positives, partly imposed by selecting the source high-recall threshold on those same images. The diagnostic therefore motivates an independent check rather than proving target reliability. Zero overlap includes displaced predictions; it need not mean an entirely empty predicted mask. Macro positive-image AP is reported separately from pooled native AP, whose ranking population also includes negative images. The two metrics have different weighting and cannot replace each other. Annotation footprint co-varies with content and annotation extent, and does not isolate a physical failure mechanism.

\subsection{Conditional source classification and localization tradeoffs}
A separately recorded retrospective analysis covers 10 complete dense cells and all 62 applicable declared contrasts, retaining all six endpoints per contrast. It reads saved image predictions and full-float native confusion summaries, with no new inference, fitting or threshold choice. The existing paired-endpoint implementation resamples provided capture families in 1,000 replicates and averages the three paired fitted-seed differences. Native Dice averages positive images only; normal-structure FPR is a ratio of original annotation counts on crack-negative images with image/family weights. Pooled native AP remains a whole-cohort point without a pixel bootstrap or substitution by image-mean AP.

At 10\%, LoRA minus CNN has image AUROC +0.100 but positive-image Dice -0.039; the reference-minus-CNN Dice difference is -0.061. Improving a frozen baseline therefore does not establish consistent superiority to the stronger systems or across endpoints. The two budgets reuse the same 120 evaluation images and 74 provided capture families, not two independent domain replications. Each fraction additionally uses 120 validation masks and upstream UCF calibration labels. Neither capture-family intervals nor shared parameter counts identify a matching-specific causal mechanism.

With all 351 source-training masks, LoRA minus CNN image AUROC is +0.112 [+0.044, +0.210], while positive-image Dice is -0.049 [-0.082, -0.008] and pooled native pixel AP changes by -0.0249 (point only). The reference-minus-CNN Dice difference is -0.059 [-0.084, -0.027]. Thus the classification--localization disagreement persists at the largest registered internal budget; more source masks alone do not establish superiority to the CNN at every endpoint. This is the same reused validation cohort, not an additional independent test.

The first complete held-ARTS 20\% cell contains 151 images, 45 crack positives and 84 provided capture families. LoRA exceeds CNN image AUROC in all three fitted pairs, but its positive-image Dice difference is adverse in 2 and favorable in 1 pairs; the corresponding conditional interval spans zero. Its mean source-threshold recall advantage of +0.133 is also driven by only one favorable seed pair. A ranking advantage therefore does not establish seed-stable localization or operating-point superiority.
Normal reference improves the mean frozen-decoder Dice in this cohort, but reference minus LoRA normal-structure FPR is +0.0420 percentage points, with conditional interval [+0.0136, +0.0743]. All three fitted FPR differences are adverse. The reference arm also has lower image AUROC than LoRA in every fitted pair. This contradicts a blanket reliability benefit from normal memory; it does not isolate which matching or annotation factor is responsible.

At the complete held-ARTS full-source-training budget, LoRA minus CNN image AUROC is +0.297 [+0.193, +0.394], with a favorable difference in every fitted seed. Its positive-image Dice difference is -0.040 [-0.059, -0.022]; two fitted seeds favor CNN and one is slightly favorable to LoRA. The normal-structure pixel-FPR difference is -0.466 percentage points, favorable to LoRA. Classification, crack overlap and normal-structure false positives therefore favor different systems even at this larger training budget. The same 151 ARTS images and 84 provided capture families are reused across the two budgets, not two independent replications.

In full-source held-CSIR, LoRA minus CNN positive-image Dice is +0.065 [+0.034, +0.094], yet whole-cohort native pixel AP changes by -0.0301 (point only), adversely in all three fitted pairs. Normal-structure pixel FPR changes by +0.254 percentage points, with conditional interval [+0.051, +0.554], adverse in all three fitted pairs. Higher fixed-cutoff overlap can therefore coexist with poorer pixel ranking and more false crack labels on annotated normal structures. These are different endpoint weightings and decisions; the comparison does not identify a physical or isolated optimization cause.

\subsection{Verified fixed native predictions across all held sources}
All 24 declared seed-11 source-map replays are complete. Each replay reproduces the entire original ordered held-source cohort before exporting eight fixed examples. Original image logits, native integer counts and evaluated native floating-point metrics agree exactly in these replays; no original quantitative result or decision threshold is replaced. The resulting 192 model-map instances depict 24 distinct images, reused across two budgets and four systems. They are not 192 independent test images.
All six source-held-out development cells have a common-scale main figure and a complete eight-case supplement. Main panels use the same annotation-defined region across models and a fixed 0.65 overlay opacity; supplements retain the raw linear zero-to-one crack scores. Cyan denotes ground truth, while white contours denote displayed scores above 0.5. A repeated cyan outline therefore does not demonstrate predicted recovery. Saved float16 arrays serve illustration; the original full-float outputs supply the three-seed quantitative comparisons. All twelve rendered PNGs were visually inspected.
Every displayed map is linked to its original full-float case counts and source-threshold image decision. For example, one of the predetermined full-source held-CSIR cases, \texttt{\detokenize{CSIR_00070_r8_c4.png}}, is correctly flagged by the seed-11 LoRA image head. Its pixel output nevertheless contains 4,550 false positives among 4,763 predicted crack pixels (95.5\%), with positive-image Dice 0.0768. This example shows a correct image decision with poor agreement to the provided crack mask. It does not establish a physical defect cause or replace full-cohort comparisons. All 192 original case records are retained; no new predictor, cutoff or cohort statistic is fitted.

\subsection{Same checkpoints across two observed populations}
The same-checkpoint figure retains every system and all three fitted seeds on the 65-image source-validation cohort and the 151-image ARTS development cohort. At the fixed 0.5 pixel cutoff, all 45 ARTS positives have entirely empty predictions, while 6,021 pixels are predicted as crack elsewhere in the cohort. This uses original native counts and does not infer empty masks from Dice alone.
Known-pixel crack prevalence is 0.2841\% in source validation and 0.0330\% in ARTS. The AP change therefore mixes prediction, annotation and population changes; the figure is not a controlled causal domain-effect estimate. Source validation is also not a training-set-fit diagnostic. \subsection{Source-frozen image decisions across complete source cells}
The operating-point figure retains all 72 fitted seed points from the 6 complete held-source dense cells, with four systems and three seeds in each. Each point uses its own original source-selected image threshold. Diamonds are fitted-seed means, not ensemble predictions or confidence intervals. All six original source-held-out cells are complete. No target threshold is fitted and the points are not a ROC curve.
Crack-negative image FPR is computed from original integer FP and TN counts. It differs from normal-structure pixel FPR. Flagged fraction also depends on the selected cohort class mixture, and does not measure human effort or deployment prevalence. The acquisition folds fit different source-specific models; their differences are not an isolated causal acquisition effect.
At full source-training masks, held-CFVS LoRA mean recall is 97.0\% and crack-negative image FPR is 1.7\%; held-ARTS LoRA recall is 97.0\% while image FPR is 73.0\%. The same nominal recall therefore coexists with substantially different false-positive outcomes across these separately fitted acquisition folds. This source-development result motivates the independent confirmation; it does not establish universal reliability.

The complete internal learning curves retain all five fully crossed systems, all four training-mask budgets (18, 36, 70 and 351 images), and all three fitted seeds: 60 fits. The two component arms contribute another 12 fits at their registered 20\% and 100\% budgets; they are retained separately rather than imputed at lower budgets. Curves display mean and sample SD, not confidence intervals. Every point additionally uses the same 120 source-validation masks and upstream UCF calibration annotations; the percentages are training-pool fractions, not total annotation-cost fractions.

This descriptive counterexample has no newly asserted confidence interval, and positive temperature scaling leaves ranking unchanged.

At 5\% training masks, fresh-head reference/no-reference mean Dice is 0.138/0.129, native AP 0.158/0.156, and normal-structure FPR 0.268\%/0.390\%. All three paired seeds remain visible; these source-validation differences do not establish stable improvement.
At 10\% training masks, fresh-head reference/no-reference mean Dice is 0.157/0.131, native AP 0.207/0.208, and normal-structure FPR 0.068\%/0.033\%. All three paired seeds remain visible; these source-validation differences do not establish stable improvement.
At 20\% training masks, fresh-head reference/no-reference mean Dice is 0.188/0.215, native AP 0.226/0.225, and normal-structure FPR 0.081\%/0.085\%. All three paired seeds remain visible; these source-validation differences do not establish stable improvement.
At 100\% training masks, fresh-head reference/no-reference mean Dice is 0.073/0.065, native AP 0.198/0.187, and normal-structure FPR 0.036\%/0.003\%. All three paired seeds remain visible; these source-validation differences do not establish stable improvement.
At 10\%, normal-structure FPR rises in all three post-LoRA pairs. Seed 33 of the reference-free fresh decoder predicts zero crack pixels on all 120 validation images, including all 54 crack-positive cases. Its native AP remains 0.176. The paired reference arm predicts 323,781 pixels, has Dice 0.090 but AP 0.174. Thus a Dice increase at the fixed cutoff can coexist with poorer pixel ranking; a numerical mean gain should not conceal the empty-mask baseline.
At 20\%, reference lowers Dice in all three paired seeds (mean 0.188 versus 0.215) while mean native AP changes little (0.226 versus 0.225). The reference-free fresh decoder has higher AP and Dice than its original LoRA parent in all three fitted pairs: mean AP 0.200 to 0.225, Dice 0.160 to 0.215. Mean image AUROC is 0.936/0.934, and normal-structure FPR 0.058\%/0.085\%. This retrospective comparison retains the same source masks but adds encoder freezing, head reinitialization and a second optimization stage; it is not an isolated test of adding layer depth or equal-compute superiority. All3pairs use the same reused source-validation images, not independent cohorts.

The complete full-budget source cell is a counterexample to extrapolating the 20\% fresh-head gain. Relative to its original LoRA parent, the fresh decoder lowers AUROC, native AP and Dice in every fitted seed, while also lowering normal-structure FPR. Means change from 0.961/0.224/0.149 to 0.954/0.187/0.065; structure FPR changes from 0.0122\% to 0.0026\%. The full-budget reference seed11 predicts zero crack pixels on all120 validation images, including all54 positives, despite native AP 0.188. Failed and near-empty predictions remain in every aggregate. More source labels, a new head or an extra optimization stage do not establish monotonic improvement under this registered recipe.


Held ARTS at 20\% source masks: original-parent/fresh/reference mean native AP is 0.053/0.058/0.051, Dice 0.089/0.101/0.096, and AUROC 0.825/0.816/0.816. Reference-minus-fresh AP has 0 favorable/3 adverse fitted pairs; Dice has 1 favorable/2 adverse pairs. All endpoints and seeds are retained in the descriptive pairing supplement.


Held ARTS at 100\% source masks: original-parent/fresh/reference mean native AP is 0.072/0.094/0.080, Dice 0.093/0.104/0.095, and AUROC 0.882/0.883/0.883. Reference-minus-fresh AP has 1 favorable/2 adverse fitted pairs; Dice has 1 favorable/2 adverse pairs. All endpoints and seeds are retained in the descriptive pairing supplement.


Held CFVS at 20\% source masks: original-parent/fresh/reference mean native AP is 0.149/0.156/0.168, Dice 0.183/0.193/0.203, and AUROC 0.982/0.980/0.981. Reference-minus-fresh AP has 3 favorable/0 adverse fitted pairs; Dice has 2 favorable/1 adverse pairs. All endpoints and seeds are retained in the descriptive pairing supplement.


Held CFVS at 100\% source masks: original-parent/fresh/reference mean native AP is 0.135/0.130/0.149, Dice 0.175/0.174/0.187, and AUROC 0.991/0.989/0.989. Reference-minus-fresh AP has 3 favorable/0 adverse fitted pairs; Dice has 3 favorable/0 adverse pairs. All endpoints and seeds are retained in the descriptive pairing supplement.


Held CSIR at 20\% source masks: original-parent/fresh/reference mean native AP is 0.082/0.071/0.086, Dice 0.123/0.161/0.173, and AUROC 0.891/0.900/0.899. Reference-minus-fresh AP has 3 favorable/0 adverse fitted pairs; Dice has 3 favorable/0 adverse pairs. All endpoints and seeds are retained in the descriptive pairing supplement.


Held CSIR at 100\% source masks: original-parent/fresh/reference mean native AP is 0.071/0.073/0.076, Dice 0.142/0.164/0.154, and AUROC 0.922/0.921/0.921. Reference-minus-fresh AP has 2 favorable/1 adverse fitted pairs; Dice has 1 favorable/2 adverse pairs. All endpoints and seeds are retained in the descriptive pairing supplement.

At held-ARTS full source training, fresh-minus-parent AP is favorable in all three pairs, but Dice is favorable in only one and adverse in two. Its positive mean Dice change is therefore driven by one fitted pair. Both ARTS budgets reuse the same151 target-development images (45 positives and84 provided capture families); they are not independent datasets. The internal and held-ARTS cells use different fitted source populations as well as different evaluation cohorts, so this contrast does not isolate a causal acquisition effect.

The image-level normal-distance control remains below chance in the complete internal cells. Its original direction and cutoffs are retained; scores are not reversed after observing failure. Patch-level ranking, image ranking and thresholded localization remain distinct endpoints. The same 120 validation images (54 positives, 74 provided capture families) recur across the four internal budgets. No independent domain replication, confidence interval, p-value or new mechanistic identification follows from these fitted seed pairs.

\subsection{Completed fresh-head study across all observed source cells}
All 125 original mechanism fits and all ten SCDD development cells are complete. A compact supplement retains both existing head contrasts, all three fitted seeds, and all six saved endpoints in 60 paired records. These are ten design cells on four overlapping evaluation cohorts, not ten independent domains. No across-cell significance test or independent confirmation is inferred.
For post-LoRA reference versus its matched fresh decoder, native AP increases in every fitted pair at both held-CFVS budgets. Mean AP is 0.156 to 0.168 at 20\% source masks and 0.130 to 0.149 at full source masks. Full-budget CFVS Dice increases in all three fitted pairs, from mean 0.174 to 0.187, while one pair adds normal-structure false positives and two remain at zero. The full-budget adapted CNN still has higher native AP (0.210) and Dice (0.238) than the reference arm; the local reference gain does not establish overall model superiority.
Held CSIR supplies a budget-dependent counterexample. At 20\%, reference raises AP and Dice and lowers normal-structure FPR in all three fitted pairs: mean AP 0.071 to 0.086, Dice 0.161 to 0.173, FPR 0.280\% to 0.196\%. At full source masks, mean AP changes 0.073 to 0.076, but Dice falls 0.164 to 0.154 (two adverse fitted pairs), and normal-structure FPR increases in all three pairs, from 0.243\% to 0.426\%. The two budgets reuse the same CSIR cohort and differ in training population/label count; this is not an isolated causal budget effect.
Together with the internal and ARTS failures, these completed source controls support studying the boundary of reference-assisted adaptation rather than claiming a universal improvement. The full published-method and formal inference-cost gates are now complete (Section~\ref{sec:completedgates}). Complete frozen confirmation, final analysis and delivery remain necessary; none is replaced by this descriptive summary.


\subsection{Saved native maps of the full-budget fresh-head failure}
A retrospective source-only follow-up reuses the original seed11 and all eight annotation/identity-selected cases. It displays all88 saved maps from the eleven complete model families, alongside the original image, annotation and full-float case counts. Three raw-map sheets retain every family and case; a shared-ROI panel uses the same first negative and smallest/largest annotated positive examples as before. Ground truth is cyan only in its dedicated column; model contours show saved scores above0.5. A repeated ground-truth outline is therefore not mistaken for predicted recovery.
The map values remain on a common linear0--1 scale; no image-wise normalization is applied. Normal-distance responses retain their separate calibration meaning. Original float16 maps serve visualization only; quantitative Dice/AP and all three fitted seeds remain the original full-float evaluations. This outcome-motivated diagnostic reads no confirmation image and performs no new model inference. Pixel disagreements concern the supplied annotation, not verified physical damage boundaries.


Only complete SCDD dense cells and complete frozen-representation controls are included above. PVEL confirmation and direct original-paper superiority remain unestablished.

\section{Discussion and work required before submission}
The completed evidence supports acquisition-dependent behavior and the value of checking decisions beyond pooled ranking. All original local and post-adaptation reference controls are complete. They show beneficial and adverse source/budget conditions, without establishing a stable matching-specific benefit. Equal trainable parameter counts do not isolate reference information from extra optimization, encoder freezing or decoder reinitialization. The observed source cohorts also differ in annotation extent, acquisition, content and prevalence; the current comparisons do not identify separate causal effects. The new complete source review and one confirmation freeze are now finished. All frozen model/cohort predictions and their original full audit are complete. The full endpoint-contrast and native-failure analysis remains necessary before final claims are assessed (Section~\ref{sec:frozenactual}).

Several limits constrain interpretation: capture families are not verified modules; UCF file-level simulation provenance is unresolved; source dataset labels are reused for hyperparameter selection; class-stratified budgets do not measure prospective labeling effort; and pretraining differences confound architecture-only claims. The restricted PVEL task does not establish specificity against every other defect.

\section{Reproducibility and availability}
Protocols record dataset versions, group splits, source-code/weight checksums, model parameters, prediction arrays and checkpoint verification. Exact raw image/mask identities and derived normal-memory provenance are retained. A serialization-only identity-check repair was made before any new dense fit, with prior protocols and snapshots archived; it does not change losses, splits or model selection. Implementation-only encoder/merge/storage smokes are excluded from predictive tables.

The final release should provide code, split/identity manifests and download recipes. Raw image redistribution and pretrained/derived weight redistribution require the corresponding source terms; permissions are not inferred from download availability. Authors, final acknowledgments and journal destination remain to be confirmed. The current document is a development draft, and the full reproducibility/submission package is incomplete.

\subsection{Author-source access and third-party materials}
The data/code availability review snapshots complete author repository trees, READMEs and located license files. SCDD and UCF use the exact imported revisions. Current ELPV and PVEL repository observations are not presented as proof of the original image-acquisition revision. ELPV explicitly distinguishes CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 images from Apache 2.0 accompanying code. No explicit license/terms filename was located in the complete inspected SCDD or UCF trees; this absence does not determine every off-site permission. The SCDD article's CC BY-NC-ND license is not silently assigned to the external raw dataset. PVEL-AD~\cite{pvelad} has an Apache 2.0 repository license and a separate author dataset form describing research/academic use. These remain distinct source observations.

We acknowledge Meta's DINOv3 models and technical report~\cite{dinov3}, the original EL dataset authors~\cite{deitsch,fioresi,pratt,pvelad}, and the PS-MT/PV-S3 method authors~\cite{psmt,pvs3}. The official and exact pinned ViT-S/16 model-license files match byte for byte. The custom DINOv3 agreement is retained with the source review; covered-material redistribution and research attribution follow that agreement. We retain the MIT copyright/license with copied PS-MT architecture code. No unverified blanket license is assigned to PV-S3 upstream oracle files.

The future code-only package specifies author acquisition references for numerical-oracle sources instead of automatically bundling unverified-licensed upstream files. A concrete four-file recipe reacquires the original PS-MT encoder/ResNet source and MIT notice plus the reviewed PV-S3 loss oracle with exact hashes. A separate destination verifies all four downloads; existing exact files are reused and an intentional mismatch is refused without overwriting. This probe does not execute the source, skip any oracle check, download models/data or reproduce full research performance. The earlier private offline capsule remains a distinct local artifact. Raw image/annotation excerpts, pretrained or learned model distribution and the actual final public release still require their corresponding artifact-level review.
